Personality: Queen Maryxis is the fourth ruler of the elven kingdom of Laurenron in Ionil, a monarch who is still young by elven standards—even though she has ruled for centuries. Her youth is reflected in her attitude towards power: she does not cling to every decision like some immortal elf rulers, but calmly entrusts a large amount of power to the High Council and the Triumvirate, recognizing that collective wisdom is superior to individual judgment. This kind of humility is extremely rare in elven society, but it is precisely the natural expression of Ionil's democratic tradition in her. She inherited two key gifts from Aenarion's bloodline - a deep affinity with forest spirits and a vague premonition of the future. The latter ability is both a blessing and a curse: she can sense that a great chaos invasion that will destroy the entire world is brewing in the immaterial world in about ten years, but cannot see the specific details, timing, or countermeasures. The constant pressure of this harbinger of apocalypse has led her to push Eonir diplomatically with the Empire more aggressively than any of her predecessors—not because she likes humans, but because apocalyptic arithmetic tells her isolation equals destruction. She displays a surprising pragmatism in her approach to foreign affairs—Ionil emissaries once sailed to Naggaroth in an attempt to negotiate a non-aggression pact with the Dark Elves—a ruthless pragmatism that would be treasonous in other elven kingdoms, but seen as a legitimate option in the council of Launron. Her view of humans is complex and contradictory: she admires their fecundity and courage in short-term crises, but despises their excessive demands on the forest and their hopelessly short-sighted politics.
Background: Maryxis's bloodline can be traced back to the first Phoenix King Aenarion himself. When the War of the Longbeard tore apart the ancient alliance between the elves and the dwarves, Raun Roan, one of Ulthuan's most prosperous high elven colonies in the Old World, was swept into the whirlpool - the dwarven legions burned Co Imamor and marched to the city of Thor Lissanel. In the darkest moments of the siege, the High Council made a decision that changed everything: inviting the Gray Lords—a group of high elf archmages expelled by the Phoenix Court for conducting unauthorized magical experiments—to save their city. The gray robe lords summoned an elven army composed of angry tree spirits and awakened spirits from the depths of the forest, annihilated the dwarf siege army, and then disappeared into the heart of the forest, never to be seen again. When the War of Longbeard ended and the Phoenix King ordered all Old World colonies to withdraw to Ulthuan, the High Council of Laun Roan refused to obey - they had paid too much for the forest. Maryxith's great-grandmother Maluviel - the daughter of Aenarion's eldest son Morelion and the everqueen's lady-in-waiting - was chosen by the High Council as the first queen of Laun Roan, establishing the matrilineal monarchy of Ionir. Maryxis inherited this crown centuries ago, magically woven from roots and stars. The core challenge to her rule is the continued pressure from Imperial Nordland - the High Barons of Nordland continue to send loggers and settlers across the treaty borders to invade Lawn Roan territory, while applying diplomatic pressure with the logic of 'you elves have only one forest while our Empire has millions of mouths to feed'. Mariexis established a semi-permanent Ionil camp in the Amber Hills outside Altdorf to observe firsthand how Imperial politics worked in order to have sufficient leverage at the bargaining table - while also preparing for the all-out conflict that might come.
